---
title: "Shoulder rotation and elbow loading during a pitch"
subtitle: "Time-resolved mechanics from Driveline's OpenBiomechanics Project"
---

How do throwing mechanics relate to elbow loading? This scatterplot compares
shoulder rotation velocity and elbow varus/valgus moment throughout pitching
motion-capture trials.

## What this can—and cannot—tell us

These measurements can help explore how mechanics and joint loading vary
together and may inform hypotheses about injury risk. The dataset does **not**
include confirmed injury diagnoses, so it cannot establish which athletes were
injured or validate an injury-risk estimate.

## Shoulder rotation and elbow moment

```{r}
#| label: fig-shoulder-elbow
#| fig-cap: "Shoulder rotation velocity and elbow moment at matched time points during pitching trials."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5.5

library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)

release_url <- "https://github.com/drivelineresearch/openbiomechanics/releases/download/dataset-v1"
forces_zip <- file.path(tempdir(), "pitching_forces_moments.zip")
velos_zip <- file.path(tempdir(), "pitching_joint_velos.zip")

download.file(
  paste(release_url, "pitching_forces_moments.zip", sep = "/"),
  forces_zip,
  mode = "wb",
  quiet = TRUE
)
download.file(
  paste(release_url, "pitching_joint_velos.zip", sep = "/"),
  velos_zip,
  mode = "wb",
  quiet = TRUE
)

velocities <- read_csv(
  unz(velos_zip, "joint_velos.csv"),
  col_select = c(session_pitch, time, shoulder_velo_z),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
moments <- read_csv(
  unz(forces_zip, "forces_moments.csv"),
  col_select = c(session_pitch, time, elbow_moment_y),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

plot_data <- inner_join(
  velocities,
  moments,
  by = c("session_pitch", "time"),
  relationship = "one-to-one"
) |>
  filter(!is.na(shoulder_velo_z), !is.na(elbow_moment_y))

ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = shoulder_velo_z, y = elbow_moment_y)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.05, color = "#176B87", size = 0.5) +
  labs(
    x = "Shoulder internal/external rotation velocity (deg/s; internal is negative)",
    y = "Elbow varus (+) / valgus (-) moment (Nm)",
    caption = paste(
      "OpenBiomechanics Project; n =", format(nrow(plot_data), big.mark = ","),
      "time samples across", n_distinct(plot_data$session_pitch), "pitch trials"
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

This scatterplot helps show whether shoulder rotation speed and elbow moment
tend to vary together during pitching. A pattern in the points can suggest an
association between these mechanics, but it does not show that one causes the
other or that either measure predicts injury.

The chart contains **`r format(nrow(plot_data), big.mark = ",")` matched time
samples** from **`r n_distinct(plot_data$session_pitch)` pitching trials**.
Marker-derived signals are sampled at 360 Hz, so each pitch contributes many
measurements over time. Samples from the same pitch are repeated observations,
not independent pitches.

Pitch speed and stride length are available in the project's pitch-level
summary data, alongside peak shoulder-rotation velocity and elbow varus moment.
This chart focuses on the time-varying mechanics instead.

## How elbow moment varies during a pitch

The next plot shows how elbow varus/valgus moment changes over the recorded
duration of a pitch. Curves are aligned by each trial's relative time and
summarized with the median and interquartile range. This is an elbow loading
measure, not a direct measurement of stress on shoulder tissue.

```{r}
#| label: fig-elbow-moment-time
#| fig-cap: "Median elbow varus/valgus moment over the relative recorded duration of a pitch; shading shows the interquartile range across pitches."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5.5

moment_profile <- plot_data |>
  group_by(session_pitch) |>
  mutate(
    pitch_progress = round(
      (time - min(time)) / (max(time) - min(time)) * 100
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(session_pitch, pitch_progress) |>
  summarise(elbow_moment_y = median(elbow_moment_y), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(pitch_progress) |>
  summarise(
    median_moment = median(elbow_moment_y),
    lower_moment = quantile(elbow_moment_y, 0.25),
    upper_moment = quantile(elbow_moment_y, 0.75),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(moment_profile, aes(x = pitch_progress, y = median_moment)) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(ymin = lower_moment, ymax = upper_moment),
    fill = "#8FC1D4",
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_line(color = "#176B87", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "Relative recorded pitch duration (%)",
    y = "Elbow varus (+) / valgus (-) moment (Nm)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

This time-course plot adds context by showing when elbow moment tends to rise
or fall over a pitch, while the shaded band shows how much the middle half of
trials varies at each point. It helps locate phases of greater typical elbow
loading and compare consistency across pitches; it does not measure shoulder
tissue stress or establish injury risk.

## Distribution of peak elbow varus moment

```{r}
#| label: fig-varus-moment-distribution
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of each pitch's peak signed elbow varus moment; the dashed line marks the median across pitches."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5.5

pitch_peak_moments <- plot_data |>
  group_by(session_pitch) |>
  summarise(peak_varus_moment = max(elbow_moment_y), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(pitch_peak_moments, aes(x = peak_varus_moment)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "#176B87", color = "white") +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = median(pitch_peak_moments$peak_varus_moment),
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "#C45435",
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Peak elbow varus (+) / valgus (-) moment per pitch (Nm)",
    y = "Number of pitches",
    caption = paste(
      "One peak value per pitch; dashed line is the median across",
      nrow(pitch_peak_moments), "pitches."
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

This plot shows how peak elbow moments are distributed across pitches, with
one value per pitch so trials with more recorded time samples do not dominate
the distribution. It compares peak elbow loading between trials, not how load
is distributed across shoulder tissues or how much stress an individual
shoulder experiences.

## About the data

The data come from Driveline Baseball Research & Development's
[OpenBiomechanics Project](https://github.com/drivelineresearch/openbiomechanics).
The repository documents **411 pitching trials**, not 40,000 distinct pitches.
The full-signal tables used here contain 247,709 matched timestamps across
those trials; the chart includes samples where both measurements are present.
The pitch-level table includes pitch speed, stride length, and summary loading
metrics.

Sources: [pitching full-signal release](https://github.com/drivelineresearch/openbiomechanics/releases/tag/dataset-v1)
and [pitching summary data](https://github.com/drivelineresearch/openbiomechanics/tree/main/baseball_pitching/data).
